_why: Cases the harness cannot measure. Each entry states the reason; none is a silent skip. A quarantined case is still counted in the digest, so it cannot be forgotten. All four entries are one class: a <meta refresh> short enough to fire mid-analysis. Blink tears down the execution context as soon as it BEGINS navigating, so aborting the request at the network layer is too late, and Chromium has no equivalent of the accessibility.blockautorefresh preference the legacy harness set for exactly this. Freezing time through CDP Emulation.setVirtualTimePolicy would likely work, and is rejected on balance: it would alter timing behaviour across all 8 465 cases to rescue 4. Measured: 94 fixtures carry a meta refresh, only these 4 have a delay under 3 seconds.

cases.rules/META_REFRESH_WO_DELAY/true/1.html#: zero-delay <meta refresh>: Blink tears down the execution context as soon as it begins navigating, before any analysis can run. Aborting the request at the network layer is too late, and Chromium has no equivalent of the accessibility.blockautorefresh preference the legacy harness set for exactly this. Observed to wedge a run intermittently (41 min of wall clock for 47 s of CPU, orphaned renderers).
cases.rules/META_REFRESH_WO_DELAY/true/2.html#: same: <meta http-equiv=refresh content=0> reloading the page onto itself.
cases.sets/38766/13-1-2-38766_2.html#38766: zero-delay <meta refresh> to a sibling page. INTERMITTENT, which is worse than a clean failure: run 1 of S3 recorded ERROR, run 2 recorded na, same code and same corpus. A tier that flakes one run in two never becomes a blocking gate. Coverage lost: criterion 38766 keeps its 'no refresh' and 'delayed refresh' fixtures but loses the immediate one — the branch this criterion is about.
cases.sets-debug/21717/24-21717_2.html#21717: same class, S4 tier. Quarantined pre-emptively rather than waiting for it to flake a nightly run.
